questions.q: Why is collation one of the most expensive settings to change after installation?
options: Collation only affects the GUI language, not any data
It's actually cheap to change — a single sp_configure command fixes it
Changing it effectively means rebuilding system databases and often reloading user data, since it affects how master, model, msdb, and tempdb compare data
Collation can be changed per-query with no instance-wide impact
questions.explain: Collation affects character comparisons throughout the system databases themselves, which is why it's one of the pre-install decisions worth getting right the first time.

questions.q: What is the recommended best practice for SQL Server service accounts?
options: Always use Local System for every service to simplify configuration
Share one domain administrator account across all SQL Server services
Service accounts don't matter and can be assigned randomly
A dedicated least-privilege account per service, such as a domain gMSA — never Local System
questions.explain: A dedicated least-privilege account limits what a compromised service can leverage and allows independent auditing per service.

questions.q: Why is it recommended to plan separate storage paths for data files, log files, and tempdb before install?
options: Log files can only be created after data files already exist
The transaction log is written sequentially and benefits from dedicated low-latency I/O, while data file access is far more random
It has no real performance benefit, only organizational convenience
SQL Server will refuse to install unless files are on separate disks
questions.explain: Separating log I/O (sequential) from data I/O (random) on different storage avoids contention that hurts both workloads.

questions.q: What does MAXDOP planning involve, per this lesson?
options: Deciding how much disk space tempdb should occupy
Deciding the server's collation
Deciding which edition of SQL Server to install
Deciding how many CPU cores a single query's parallel execution plan can use, based on core count and workload
questions.explain: MAXDOP governs parallelism per query, and the right value depends on core count and whether the workload is OLTP or reporting-heavy.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend estimating a year or two of database growth during planning, rather than just current size?
options: It has no practical effect and is purely a documentation exercise
Undersized files that autogrow constantly in small increments fragment storage and cause pauses during growth events
Growth estimates only matter for tempdb, not user databases
SQL Server requires you to specify final database size at install time and can never grow files afterward
questions.explain: Realistic starting sizes avoid the fragmentation and growth-event pauses that come from relying on small default autogrowth increments.
